about.quote: “Explore the cultural soul of Cameroon, region by region”
about.intro: MboaTrip is a tourism and community platform dedicated to discovering Cameroon, region by region. Today: the West (Bandjoun, Bafoussam) and the Littoral (Douala) — royal chiefdoms, urban heritage, local gastronomy, hotels and restaurants — with new regions added progressively. The goal: help travelers explore every corner of the country, while sharing their own experiences with a community of enthusiasts.
about.exploreText: An interactive map to discover the tourist sites, hotels and restaurants of every region already covered by MboaTrip.
about.shareText: Post your travel photos: the place you visited, a caption, the date — to keep a record and inspire others.
about.commentText: React to other travelers' posts and mark whether a comment was helpful with 👍🏽👎🏽 votes.
about.saveText: Bookmark your favorite places to easily find them again later.
about.communityText: MboaTrip isn't just a guide — it's also a space where every traveler can document their visits and help others better prepare for theirs, one place at a time.

home.heroSubtitle: Royal chiefdoms, museums, food and Bamiléké hospitality — to discover before you even arrive.
home.searchPlaceholder: Search for a site, hotel, or restaurant...
home.cultureText1: Bandjoun and Bafoussam are two major chiefdoms of Bamiléké country, in the Grassfields of Western Cameroon. Royal palaces adorned with carvings, wood and raffia craftsmanship, indigo-dyed Ndop cloth, and an ancestral social organization still alive around the figure of the Fo (traditional chief).
home.cultureText2: Each chiefdom has its own ceremonial huts, secret societies, and skills passed down from generation to generation.
home.lionAlt: Lion, a symbol of Bamiléké heritage
home.gastronomySubtitle: Tap a dish to see all its photos.
home.craftsFootnote: Generic photos (illustrating the craft) — no royalty-free photo specific to Bandjoun/Bafoussam workshops found so far.
home.hotelsSubtitle: Real selection (Tripadvisor / Booking.com), with ratings and reviews. Tap for details.
home.hotelsFootnote: Real photos of Tagidor Garden Resort and La Vallée de Bana. Hotel Altitel: generic photo pending a reliable source.
home.restaurantsFootnote: Real data (Google ratings and reviews). Real photos available for La Terrasse, ASAT and Happy Land (source: Ayila'a) — other establishments don't have a verified photo yet.
home.eventsText: Coming soon — festivals, traditional dances and craft markets in the region.
home.mapCtaTitle: The whole region, one interactive map
home.mapCtaText: Tourist sites, hotels, restaurants and hospitals precisely located — powered by OpenStreetMap, 100% free.
home.cultureSawaText1: Douala, Cameroon's economic capital, is above all the land of the Sawa people — literally “the people of the water”. Their culture revolves around the Wouri river, fishing, and the worship of water oracles, embodied notably by the Ngondo, the great traditional Sawa assembly.
home.cultureSawaText2: The Palace of Sawa Culture (Mukanda mwa Ngondo), built in the shape of a dugout canoe, and the Dika Akwa Nya Bonambella Palace keep alive today the memory of the Akwa dynasty and Sawa traditions, between colonial heritage and contemporary cultural expression.
home.newBellAlt: La Nouvelle Liberté, the iconic statue at Deido roundabout in Douala
home.gastronomySawaSubtitle: Tap a dish to see all its photos.
